1584: Then to the clothes of the men, stripping off their black coats, smashing down glossy stove pipe hats, scattering around panamas, sombreros, boaters, cowboy hats, lavishing flannels, linens and scarfs of silk; not interfering lightly with the garments of women, which, thanks to fashion, are generally bright enough — music in their silken rustle, glow of pink pearls and young rosebuds through the white samite of their muslin sleeves.
